newsitem.title: USA: Evergreen, Chancellor complete radio buy from Viacom.
newsitem.headline: Evergreen, Chancellor complete radio buy from Viacom.

text.p: Merger partners Evergreen Media Corp. and Chancellor Broadcasting Co. said Wednesday they completed the purchase of 10 radio stations from Viacom Inc. for $1.08 billion plus working capital.
The companies said they received Federal Communications Commission approval for the deal Friday.
An Evergreen/Chancellor spokesman said the merger of the two media companies, announced last February, is expected to close as soon as the third quarter.

The companies announced on the same day both the Viacom deal as well as their merger, which would create Chancellor Media Corp., the nation's largest pure-play radio broadcasting company with 98 stations in 21 of the nation's largest markets.
As part of the Viacom deal, Evergreen purchased two stations in New York and four in Washington for about $595 million.
Chancellor bought two stations in Los Angeles, one in Chicago and one in Detroit for about $480 million.
To comply with FCC ownership limits, Evergreen and Chancellor are unloading three of the four stations in Washington and the one in Detroit.
Evergreen's stock was unchanged at $45.125, while Chancellor was unchanged at $40.25 on Nasdaq. Viacom rose 56 cents to $30.19 on the American Stock Exchange.
